newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese bank announces $300 mln EuroCD programme.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese bank announces $300 mln EuroCD programme.

text.p: Lebanon's Byblos Bank announced a $300 million EuroCD programme on Thursday and said it would issue the first $100 million tranche in the second quarter of the year.
The notes will have five-year maturities and the issues will be managed by Merrill Lynch in association with the Dutch bank ABN AMRO, Chairman Francois Bassil told a lunch in honour of Merrill Lynch.
Further tranches will be issued as required, Bassil said.
Byblos ranked fifth among Lebanon's 82 banks last year and is considered one of the most dynamic banks in the country.

The EuroCD issue was the first announced by a Lebanese bank since international credit agencies awarded Lebanon its first ratings on Wednesday, giving it a high speculative grade which disappointed some Beirut financiers.
However, Bassil said he did not believe the ratings would affect the spread Byblos would obtain on the EuroCDs.

The bank's borrowing programme continues a trend by Lebanese banks towards international fund-raising which began last year when five banks including Byblos raised a total of $420 million in international debt.
Bankers and economists said last year that Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri was urging Lebanon's commercial banks to raise $800 million-$1 billion abroad by mid-1997.

Bassil also announced that Byblos, which ranked fifth among Lebanon's 82 banks in 1996 and increased its profits by 60 percent to $24 million, would raise its capital to $200 million within 18 months.
This will make it one of the most heavily capitalised banks in Lebanon. Capital is currently $105 million.
Bassil also said Byblos shares would be listed on the Beirut Stock Exchange in May.

The listing, which is eagerly awaited by the market, was first expected in January or February but ran into a snag over a legal requirement that 33 percent of the bank's shares remain in Lebanese hands and Byblos is having to set up a new holding company to meet the requirement.
"Our aim is to be listed by the end of May," Bassil told Reuters after the lunch.
The EuroCD programme will be Byblos's second foray into the international debt market following its $50 million three-year Euronote last September.

That issue sold out in half an hour. It was three times oversubscribed at a spread of 285 basis points over similar U.S. Treasuries. Byblos also made a successful $11.6 million international share placement in 1996.

Bassil said in reply to a question that he did not believe the credit ratings awarded to Lebanon -- Moody's B1, Standard and Poor's BB minus, IBCA's BB and Nippon's BBB minus -- would affect the spread that Byblos Bank's new issue would get.
"No, I don't think so," he said. "We were on the market before the rating. Our expectation is that we'll get a much, much better spread than the previous issue."
He said the bank would use the EuroCD funds to develop its consumer, housing and industrial credit lines and its productive investment programme.
Byblos's previous Euronote last September was managed by SBC Warburg and Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest.
Asked why Byblos had switched to Merrill Lynch, Bassil said it had held a tender to get the best offer.
"We switched to Merrill Lynch mainly because of the power of placement they have in places wherever there are Lebanese expatriates around the world. ABN AMRO have the same reach," he said.
